reason: Multivariate time series forecasting requires modeling both hierarchical temporal dynamics and complex inter-variable dependencies, a dual requirement that often degrades predictive performance and incurs high computational costs in standard Transformer architectures. Unlike current channel-independent models that ignore vital cross-variable synergies, or dense-attention frameworks that suffer from quadratic computational noise, our approach extracts structurally sparse dependencies. To address these specific limitations, this study introduces the FCA-Transformer. The proposed framework integrates a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) to isolate macroscopic trends from high-frequency localized fluctuations via hierarchical downsampling. Concurrently, a structured Transformer-based Cross-Attention (TCA) mechanism employs Dimensional Segmentation with Weighting (DSW) and a Two-Stage Attention (TSA) layer to map topological variable interactions, effectively extracting robust cross-variable pathways and mitigating distributional noise. Extensive empirical evaluations across three real-world multivariate benchmarks (ETTh1, Electricity, and Exchange Rate) demonstrate that the FCA-Transformer achieves an average reduction of up to 4.39% in MSE and 5.11% in MAE compared to leading baselines. These findings indicate that the proposed architecture successfully reconciles multi-scale feature extraction with lightweight dependency modeling, enhancing structural generalization and providing a scalable framework for real-time temporal analysis in complex industrial environments.
title: FCA-Transformer: A Feature Pyramid Time Series Forecasting Model Driven by Cross-Attention Mechanism
